purpose: Test whether source-memory CAMI adds enough benefit to result replay to justify its overhead, comparing CAMI+replay with plain+replay on already exposed development tasks.
success: All40 attempts pass fixed tests and operations; complete telemetry; uniform observed provider tier;20 expected hits and20 changed-input probes with positive controls. Plain+replay must have strictly lower four-stage token work AND charged pipeline wall in EACH of5 paired blocks. Otherwise evidence is inconclusive/unsupported; do not replace CAMI based on a favorable subset.
inputs: Original development_v2 Click tasks and frozen literal source seed; no heldout tasks or outcomes used for tuning.
runtime: Same immutable image and model Sol high as full replication; source/adapter remain a8c34cd. Exact runner/source/input pins frozen before any call.
accounting: Include canonical resets, source-memory initialization where configured, model/auth, cache lookup/record/materialization, captures, fresh fixed grading, and equal shared baseline preflight. Interleave conditions per stage and block. Each condition/block starts empty isolated source and result memory. No retries/replacement/extension/pooling.
scope: Development ablation on two previously exposed tasks, not new heldout evidence or representative production hit rates. Native model result cache remains exact-task/exact-input with fresh grading. Token work is not an invoice.
execution: Only after heldout full experiment finishes; no concurrent model experiments or changes to its immutable snapshot.
